title: Edmonton police justified in shooting David Sandaker, 24
subtitle: Murder suspect armed with semi-auto .45 had spare magazine and wore bulletproof vest
article: Edmonton police officers used reasonable force in the shooting death of an armed 24-year-old man last year, an investigation concludes.

David Charles Sandaker was wanted by police on a Canada-wide warrant as part of a murder investigation when he was spotted on a footpath in a greenspace near 51st Avenue and 149A Street in Riverbend in the early evening of May 11.
Officers in a second police vehicle saw that Sandaker had a handgun in his waistband and intentionally struck him, pinning him against a fence.
A witness reported Sandaker was trying to climb the fence.
While pinned, Sandaker began shooting at the approaching officers with the .45 caliber semi-automatic handgun, hitting one.
Police later found he had a loaded spare magazine in his back pants pocket and was wearing a bulletproof vest.
The wounded officer was hit in his lower right leg and was taken to hospital where he was treated and later released.

In a news release, Susan Hughson, executive director of the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, determined that "the officers were lawfully placed and the use of force was reasonable and justified in all the circumstances."
ASIRT's mandate is to investigate incidents involving police that resulted in serious injury or death to any person, as well as serious or sensitive allegations of police misconduct.
